name: Certificate Chain Verifier
description: Verify whether a certificate chain is trusted and unexpired, with optional hostname matching.

examples.label: Verify a chain against the root CA and check the hostname

hints.implicitTrust: There is **no system trust store** available: when no trusted root is supplied, the self-signed root inside the chain becomes an implicit anchor, so "chain is trusted" then only means the chain is internally consistent — not that it is externally trusted.
hints.result: A failed verification is a business result: the tool returns 200 with valid: false rather than an error.
hints.hostname: Hostname matching only compares names; it does not influence the chain verdict.
hints.atTime: Rolling the verification time back lets expired certificates pass; use it only to review historical signatures.

faq.q: Can a self-signed certificate pass verification?
faq.a: Yes if you supply it as a trusted root; otherwise only the implicit anchor applies, which merely proves internal consistency.

faq.q: How do I verify a certificate from a private internal CA?
faq.a: Pass the CA certificate as a trusted root.

faq.q: Does a failed verification return an error?
faq.a: No. It returns 200 with valid: false and the reasons in the errors list.
